notes: rl2:anyAgent becomes a permission without assignee; the RL2 path agent.role becomes the state property ex:requesterRole, whose value is a role instance IRI. RL2's isA maps to odrl:isA, which due2 evaluates against declared rdf:type and rdfs:subClassOf edges; the role vocabulary stays in the policy file, as RL2 requires, and only the requester's role assignment is SOTW data. RL2's value type role:Role is carried as rdfs:range: a class range requires an IRI value and otherwise documents intent, since class membership is checked only by isA (due2-profiles.md §3). The type and subclass edges are corpus data read closed-world (due2-workflows.md §3.1, §3.3): an isA that no declared chain establishes is F, never U, so scenario 3 is NotApplicable rather than Indeterminate. This relies on profiles §6 ('isA follows rdf:type and rdfs:subClassOf'); the corpus closure of workflows §3.1 lists rdf:type edges only where they type collections, so the instance's rdf:type edge is assumed to be carried too. role:Viewer and role:ViewerInstance are added to the vocabulary for scenario 3. Scenario 3 is added. No divergence from RL2.

expected.why: role:SeniorAnalystInstance is typed role:SeniorAnalyst, a subclass of role:Analyst, so isA is T. ex:analystRead has no party to match; action and target match, so it is a ready candidate.
A missing role makes the isA constraint U, so the permission is U; completions give Permit and NotApplicable.
role:ViewerInstance is typed role:Viewer, which is under role:Role but not role:Analyst, so isA is F and the permission does not apply.
